name: Peabody
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Peabody, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Peabody, MA: the downtown Holiday Stroll and City Hall tree lighting, Santa's Workshop traditions and Breakfast at the North Pole.
lede: Peabody starts Christmas with the downtown Holiday Stroll and the tree lighting in front of City Hall on Small Business Saturday, and Santa comes to breakfast at In The Game on Lowell Street.
celebrates: Peabody's season opens on Small Business Saturday with the Holiday Stroll and Tree Lighting, an afternoon downtown from 1 to 5 pm that the City of Peabody says ends with the tree lighting in front of City Hall at 4:30. At past strolls, Itemlive found Mr. and Mrs. Claus reading stories at the Peabody Institute Library, a Santa's Workshop with cookie decorating at the Knights of Columbus, a live nativity at Center Church and a reindeer scavenger hunt at the Osborn-Salata House. The Peabody Area Chamber of Commerce adds a Festival of Trees to the stroll, and In The Game Peabody serves Breakfast at the North Pole with Santa.
lastyear: In 2025 the Peabody Area Chamber of Commerce listed Peabody's Holiday Stroll and Tree Lighting for Saturday, November 29, from 1 to 5 pm downtown, the Saturday after Thanksgiving. Itemlive called the 2023 edition the city's eighth annual tree lighting and Holiday Stroll, with festive music at Courthouse Plaza, a Touch-a-Truck and Jaws of Life demonstration by the fire department, a Winter Holiday Art Fair at the library and Green Screen Fun for kids from Peabody TV.
facts: Peabody was once the South Parish of Danvers. It became the separate town of South Danvers in 1855, and on April 30, 1868, it took the name Peabody to honor George Peabody, a philanthropist born there. It became a city in 1916. Tanneries were the heart of its economy into the second half of the twentieth century, so locals still call it the Leather City or Tanner City. The Holiday Stroll is held on Small Business Saturday so families can support local shops.
trains: The MBTA Commuter Rail Newburyport/Rockport Line does not stop in Peabody. Neighboring Salem has a station on the line, with trains to North Station in Boston, and the Peabody Essex Museum sits about half a mile from that platform. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs its Holiday Express through Christmas lights. In Lowell, the National Streetcar Museum has hands-on exhibits for kids, and the Boston and Maine Railroad Historical Society displays steam locomotive No. 410 on Dutton Street.

kidfact: Peabody used to be called South Danvers. In 1868 it changed its name to Peabody to honor George Peabody, a man born there who gave his money away to help people.
faq: When is the Peabody Holiday Stroll?

The Holiday Stroll and Tree Lighting is held on Small Business Saturday, the Saturday after Thanksgiving, from 1 to 5 pm in downtown Peabody. The City of Peabody holds the tree lighting in front of City Hall at 4:30 pm, so families can spend the afternoon downtown and finish with caroling and the lights.
What do kids do at the Peabody Holiday Stroll?

At the 2023 stroll, Itemlive reported a storytime with Mr. and Mrs. Claus at the library, cookie decorating and crafts at a Santa's Workshop at the Knights of Columbus, face painting and a live nativity at Center Church, a reindeer scavenger hunt and ornament decorating at the Osborn-Salata House, and a Touch-a-Truck with the fire department.
Why is Peabody called the Tanner City?

Tanneries that made leather were the center of Peabody's economy into the second half of the twentieth century, according to the Essex National Heritage Area. They have since closed, but the city is still known locally as the Leather City or Tanner City. The name Peabody itself honors philanthropist George Peabody, who was born there.
Is there breakfast with Santa in Peabody?

Yes. In The Game Peabody, at 535 Lowell Street, hosts Breakfast at the North Pole with a hot buffet, a Christmas craft, reindeer games, a Letters to Santa station, a game play pass, prize tickets and a photo with Santa. Tickets are sold online through the venue, with children's and adults' prices listed separately.
How do I get to Peabody by train?

Peabody has no Commuter Rail stop. Take the MBTA Newburyport/Rockport Line from North Station in Boston to Salem, the neighboring city's station, and continue by bus, taxi or car. The MBTA posts a fall and winter schedule for the line, so check train times before you go.
